items.title: Soundstorm
items.description: Soundstorm is an audio-oriented federated social network that speaks ActivityPub. Users can upload their own music, comment on others' tracks, and like/follow/mention just as in a regular social network. Since it speaks the same language as federated platforms like Mastodon, Soundstorm can send new track upload posts to users' followers on the fediverse, allowing them to gain a greater reach than a conventional social audio service.

items.title: Social Relay
items.description: Social Relay is a Public post relay for Diaspora, writin in python. (Archived Project)

items.title: Mastodon
items.description: Ruby based twitter clone - Follow friends and discover new ones among more than 2M people. Publish anything you want: links, pictures, text, video. All on a platform that is community-owned and ad-free.

children.title: Hometown
children.description: a lightweight fork of Mastodon that supports local-only toots and more content types

items.description: The fediverse is made up of a bunch of protocols. Below are the most used ones.

items.title: Friendica
items.description: The Portable Contacts specification is designed to make it easier for developers to give their users a secure way to access the address books and friends lists they have built up all over the web.

items.title: DFRN
items.description: The DFRN (pronounced dee-fern) framework provides the communication basis for a decentralised social network - where cooperating servers share information on your behalf while operating in a web of trust relationships you control. It can provide a “Facebook-like” experience without requiring a central company or server.

items.title: PubSubHubbub
items.description: PubSubHubbub is an open protocol for distributed publish/subscribe communication on the Internet. It generalizes the concept of webhooks and allows data producers and data consumers to work in a decoupled way.

items.title: Pubcast
items.description: An experimental ActivityPub based podcasting platform
